classification.difficultyReason: Explain the fixed-work inverse relationship, define variables and determine the constant product, then use the resulting model to calculate either time or workforce.

content.prompt: It takes 15 people to do a job in 20 days.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain briefly why this is a suitable scenario for inverse variation.

answer.short: For a fixed job, assuming equal constant work rates, more people take fewer days and fewer people take more days; the product of people and days stays constant.
answer.worked: The amount of work is fixed. Assuming each person works at the same constant rate, doubling the number of people halves the time, so the number of people multiplied by the number of days remains constant. This is inverse variation.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Assume that the relationship is inverse variation. Form an equation that models the above scenario.

answer.short: $P=\dfrac{300}{D}$, where $P$ is the number of people and $D$ is the number of days.
answer.worked:
Let $P$ be the number of people and $D$ the number of days. Inverse variation gives $P=\dfrac{k}{D}$.
$$\begin{align*}k&=PD\\k&=15\times20\\k&=300\end{align*}$$Hence $P=\dfrac{300}{D}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence, how many days will it take 10 people to do the same job?

children.label: d
children.prompt: If it took 75 days to do the job, how many people were working on it?
